answer: Because the canyon height is fixed at intake and entered in the kernel receipt, the nebula audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 703 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That is 3 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
